summary: The group remembers: Two days after the vote, {the lobbyist} finds the player to say the group has not forgotten.
realLife: One life: After a vote on certifying an election, many companies froze donations to members who voted no. Lobbyists then told clients to rebuild ties because the members might hold leadership and committee posts, and said a blanket refusal could not last; aides to some members reportedly weighed banning lobbyists who had stopped giving. Another: One energy group would not give to members who voted against certification and another suspended giving and would review it from time to time, while a business chamber said it would not judge on that vote alone and a chemistry council reviewed members case by case. Another: Companies and trade groups gave tens of millions to state lawmakers who backed voting restrictions, and most firms that had changed giving after January 6 still gave to them. Two chairs of the legislature received money from some of the firms and did not respond; company chiefs said the right to vote was sacred without promising any action. Another: On a California city council the one member who voted against hiring a special counsel over a development said it was an election-season attack and tried to show developer contributions to his colleagues; the majority blocked his presentation, and a lobbyist's email had urged developers to keep gifts under a legal limit.
gates: The lobbying record shows {the lobbyist} met the player on a bill.
The vote record shows the player voted the other way from the group's ask.
{the lobbyist} still has a way to reach the player: a meeting, a call, or a donor on the record.
weights: How much the group gave the player before.
How much of the player's district belongs to the group.
How warmly the lobbyist and the player have dealt before.
How close the next election is.
How the lobbyist tends to say a hard thing, in a hint or out loud.
choices: thank them for the warning and explain the vote
say the vote was your own and stand on it
ask what the group wants for next time
end the talk and walk away

branches.when: the lobbyist hints that the group will remember
branches.then: The hint is written on the tie; the player decides whether to hear it as a warning or a courtesy.
The warning is written as a threat on the record and the player's reply is read later by the group and by the press.
The group may keep dealing with the player on other bills; if it does not, the explanation is said by others.

branches.when: the player refuses to be moved
branches.then: The group's giving and its endorsement follow what it decides; the donor tie is read when the next race opens.

branches.when: the group has a donor in the player's campaign
branches.then: The donor's words and gifts after the vote are read as the group's answer.
